blocks.text: The Data Collection and Understanding module ended with a dataset genuinely ready for real work, properly shaped, sourced, quality checked, leakage free, and split into training, validation, and test sets. Exploratory Data Analysis is the module that actually puts that training set to use, examining it closely before any model ever sees it, and univariate analysis is genuinely where that examination begins.

This topic covers what makes an analysis specifically univariate, the genuine tools used for numeric variables versus categorical variables, the distinction between central tendency and spread, how a single variable examined in isolation can already reveal outliers, and why this exploration should genuinely happen only on the training set, never touching validation or test.
1. What Makes an Analysis Specifically Univariate

blocks.alt: What Makes an Analysis Specifically Univariate
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993887-370277259.png

Univariate analysis genuinely means examining exactly one variable at a time, in complete isolation from every other column in the dataset. A dataset of house sales with square footage, bedrooms, and price has three columns, and a univariate analysis of price looks only at the price column, genuinely ignoring square footage and bedrooms entirely for that particular pass.

This might sound genuinely limiting at first, but it is a deliberate, valuable starting point, understanding what a single variable actually looks like on its own, its typical values, its spread, its oddities, before asking any harder question about how it relates to anything else, exactly the kind of question the Bivariate Analysis topic that follows this one takes on directly.
2. Genuine Tools for a Numeric Variable

blocks.alt: Genuine Tools for a Numeric Variable
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993888-874474934.png

A histogram is genuinely the most direct way to see the shape of a numeric variables distribution, grouping values into bins and showing how many observations fall into each one, revealing at a glance whether the data is roughly symmetric, skewed to one side, or has multiple genuine peaks. A boxplot summarizes the same variable more compactly, showing the median, the middle spread of the data, and flagging points that sit far enough outside that spread to be genuinely called outliers.

Summary statistics complete the picture numerically, the mean and median describe where values genuinely tend to cluster, while the standard deviation describes how far, on average, values genuinely scatter away from that center. Together these tools give a genuinely thorough single variable picture before anything more complex is attempted.
3. Genuine Tools for a Categorical Variable

blocks.alt: Genuine Tools for a Categorical Variable
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442993888-577374586.png

A frequency count is genuinely the starting point for any categorical variable, simply tallying how many rows fall into each distinct category. A bar chart turns that same tally into a genuinely visual comparison, making it immediately obvious which categories dominate and which are genuinely rare.

The mode, the single most frequently occurring category, is the categorical equivalent of the mean for a numeric variable, a quick, genuine summary of what a typical row looks like for that column. Spotting a category with a suspiciously large share, or one that appears only a handful of times, is often the first genuinely useful signal a univariate pass over categorical data provides.

items: Histogram: shows the genuine shape of a numeric variable distribution.
Boxplot: summarizes spread and genuinely flags outliers in a numeric variable.
Frequency count and bar chart: show how often each category genuinely appears.
Mean, median, mode, and standard deviation: numeric summaries of center and spread.

blocks.text: 4. Central Tendency Versus Spread
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442994286-91639084.png

Central tendency answers where values genuinely tend to cluster, the mean, the median, and the mode are the three genuine ways to describe a typical value. Spread answers a genuinely different question, how far values scatter away from that center, described through the range, the standard deviation, or the interquartile range, the middle fifty percent of the data.

Both questions genuinely matter, and neither one alone tells the full story, two variables can share the exact same mean while one is tightly clustered and the other is wildly spread out, a difference that only the spread half of this picture reveals, and one covered in far more numerical depth in the upcoming Statistical Summary topic.

blocks.title: A useful reminder
blocks.content: Reporting only a mean without any measure of spread genuinely hides half the picture. Two columns with an identical mean can look completely different once their spread is actually examined.

blocks.text: 5. A Worked Example
A small numeric column of house prices shows the genuine univariate toolkit in practice, using pandas for the summary statistics.

code.content:
import pandas as pd

prices = pd.Series([210000, 245000, 198000, 890000, 232000, 255000])

print("Mean:", prices.mean())
print("Median:", prices.median())
print("Standard deviation:", prices.std())
print(prices.describe())

blocks.text: The genuine gap between the mean and the median here is already a useful clue, one unusually high price is pulling the mean upward while the median stays closer to where most of the values genuinely sit, exactly the kind of single variable insight this topic is about, and exactly the kind of pattern the Distribution Analysis topic later in this module explains in much greater depth.
6. How a Single Variable Can Already Reveal Outliers

blocks.alt: How a Single Variable Can Already Reveal Outliers
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442994288-848858639.png

Even before comparing a variable to anything else, looking at it in isolation can genuinely surface outliers, values that sit far outside where most of the rest of the data lives. In the house price example above, a value of 890000 sitting well above every other price is genuinely visible immediately, both in the boxplot style view and in the gap between mean and median.

Catching outliers at this early, univariate stage matters, because an outlier left unexamined can quietly distort summary statistics, and because knowing about it here sets up the deeper treatment the dedicated Outlier Detection topic already covered elsewhere in this module goes into.
7. Explore the Training Set Only
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442994289-263369388.png

A genuinely important rule carried directly forward from the Train Validation Test Split topic, exploratory data analysis should be done exclusively on the training set, never on the validation or test sets. Looking closely at test data this early genuinely reintroduces the exact leakage risk covered earlier, letting knowledge of the test data quietly shape decisions, like which features to engineer, well before the honest final check is supposed to happen.

This restriction can feel genuinely limiting, especially when curiosity naturally wants to look at the full dataset, but respecting it here is precisely what keeps the eventual test set evaluation trustworthy, a discipline that carries through every topic in this Exploratory Data Analysis module.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Every chart and statistic in this entire Exploratory Data Analysis module should genuinely be computed from the training set alone. Peeking at validation or test data during exploration quietly undermines the honest evaluation those sets exist to provide.

blocks.text: 8. Univariate Analysis Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Univariate Analysis Versus What Comes Next
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785442994290-143403738.png

Univariate analysis genuinely answers what does this one variable look like, and that is a deliberately narrow question. Most real world patterns worth discovering involve how two or more variables genuinely move together, a question this topic was never designed to answer on its own.

The next topic, Bivariate Analysis, extends this same exploratory mindset to exactly that harder, genuinely more revealing question, examining how pairs of variables relate to each other, building directly on the single variable foundation this topic establishes.

items: Univariate analysis genuinely examines exactly one variable at a time, in isolation from the rest of the dataset.
Histograms, boxplots, and summary statistics are the genuine tools for a numeric variable.
Frequency counts, bar charts, and the mode are the genuine tools for a categorical variable.
Central tendency describes where values cluster; spread describes how far they genuinely scatter, and both matter.
A single variable examined alone can already reveal outliers worth investigating further.
Exploratory analysis should genuinely happen only on the training set, never validation or test, to avoid reintroducing leakage.
